messages:
sara_oncall: Pager — multiple customers in eu-west reporting degraded responses and increased 5xx from inference gateway. Metrics show smart-routing started sending traffic to model-quant-small instead of model-large-v2 around ~1918765400. Latency also spiked. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-492. Priority: P1. Impact: partial customer failures in eu-west. Acknowledged by sara_oncall.
pagerduty: Incident routed to rota: oncall-sre.
maria_sre: looking now — I can see a policy roll that changed fallback order for eu-west last deploy window. It moved "prefer-region" fallback to earlier in chain so when node capacity is constrained, requests fallback to quant-small.
sara_oncall: @maria_sre can you confirm whether this was an automated rollout or manual change? Customers are seeing hallucinations and timeouts.
maria_sre: It was a config push from the routing service about 1918765388 — automatic rollout with 10% canary. The canary mis-evaluated because metric-empty checks were skipped.
ryan_ops: I'm seeing a stack of backups: the canary depleted k-v-cache heat in a few pods which increased seq lengths so the scheduler thought large model couldn't serve within latency SLO and forced quant-small. That then reduced quality and caused retries -> more pressure -> more fallbacks. Cascade.
sara_oncall: OK — two questions: 1) Stop further rollouts 2) If we need to force-route to model-large-v2 in eu-west, how do we do that safely?
engmgr_jade: Lock the routing-config rollout now. I just pushed a hold. Also we should avoid global manual force for long periods. Consider temporary force-wire to a small subset of infra.
maria_sre: Suggest short mitigation: pin traffic for high-volume customers to a subset of hosts running model-large-v2 (force-model) while we heal. That avoids full rollback and keeps other customers on current path.
ryan_ops: If we do a wholesale "force-model" via the console it will set policy override across the region — that might trigger autoscaler reactions. Instead run a targeted routing rule:
```
# force large model for customer IDs in eu-west (short-lived)
redwood route apply --region eu-west --selector "customer in (acme,brightco)" --force-model model-large-v2 --ttl 10m
```
This should only affect selected tenants.
sara_oncall: Go ahead with that for the biggest impacted tenant (acme) and monitor. Maria, standby to roll back if latency creeps.
maria_sre: Applied. Confirmed acme traffic now pinned to model-large-v2. Latency dropped for that tenant, error rate dropped from 14% -> 2% within one minute.
cust_success: FYI Acme reported improved responses. They still saw a couple bad completions earlier, but overall better. Thank you.
sara_oncall: Good. Meanwhile disable the canary rollout and revert the fallback order change. Maria, can you snapshot current routing config and revert?
maria_sre: Snapshot created: rcfg-1918765432-snap. Reverting fallback-order to previous commit.
maria_sre: Revert applied, starting staged rollout to 0%. Rolling back that policy change entirely.
incident-bot: Note: manual override (force-model) detected for eu-west by ryan_ops at 1918765498. Logged in audit.
ryan_ops: After revert, we're seeing a weird loop: some hosts still route to quant-small because their local cache did not update; they hit warmup and then drop to fallback again. We need to clear KV cache on a subset; otherwise they'll keep deciding small variant.
sara_oncall: Options: a) bounce pods (risky) b) clear prefix KV cache (safer) c) widen TTL of routes to let caches expire. Which is fastest?
maria_sre: I'll hit targeted KV invalidation for the affected host pool and nudge the scheduler. Command:
```
redwood kv invalidate --region eu-west --pool pool-a --prefix "model-decisions" --confirm
```
Doing now.
maria_sre: KV invalidate completed. Observing routing convergence. Error rate trending down.
engmgr_jade: Heads-up: force-model audit shows we left a 10m TTL — keep it to 5m next time. Also capture the customer-impact window for postmortem.
sara_oncall: Agreed. Ryan, can you draft a quick impact summary for SRE/Customer Success and list customers affected and mitigation steps?
ryan_ops: On it. Draft: "Between 1918765388-1918765490 eu-west routing fallback order change caused automated fallback to quant-small for ~12% of traffic, leading to increased 5xx and degraded output quality. Mitigations: hold rollout, targeted force-model for top tenants, revert policy change, KV invalidation to converge. Effective recovery 1918765550. Customers impacted: acme (mitigated), brightco (partial), several small tenants (brief impact). Follow-ups: prevent canary skipping empty-metric checks, add circuit-breaker to avoid fallback loops, shorten default force-model TTLs."
sara_oncall: Nice. Add estimated customer-visible window and any SLO breaches. Also include links to graphs.
ryan_ops: Added SLO breach: latency p95 exceeded target for ~18 minutes for eu-west across impacted services. Including graphs: https://graphs.redwood/inci/1918765432
cust_success: We'll reach out to top customers with the mitigation note and expected RCA timeline.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-492 moved to status: mitigated. Postmortem assigned to maria_sre and ryan_ops.
sara_oncall: Closing thread here. Action items: (1) postmortem w/ timeline & root cause (maria + ryan) (2) change canary checklist to include metric-empty guard (engineering) (3) add automated detector for fallback loops (runtime team). Thanks all. :thumbsup:
